title: Proverbs 10 — The proverbs of Solomon begin: the righteous and the wicked

verdicts.reasoning: mišlê šĕlōmōh (pe) bēn ḥākām yĕśammaḥ-ʾāb ...: the heading and the in-verse petucha are verified in the source; 'Solomon' (founder point D). Exact.
Re-parsed: lōʾ-yôʿîlû ʾôṣĕrôt rešaʿ ûṣĕdāqâ taṣṣîl mimmāwet. The rendering follows the ASV sense and adds nothing. Exact.
lōʾ-yarʿîb YHWH nepeš ṣaddîq wĕhawwat rĕšāʿîm yehdōp: ASV 'soul' kept, with the appetite sense (BDB nepeš 5) in commentary; hawwâ 'craving'. Defensible.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Philologically neutral and correctly direct: a typographic convention, with the Hebrew form standing in the source text and every name verified (David, Solomon, Jerusalem, Zion, Israel, Jacob, Job). Flagged only because it is founder point D (the corpus split with the Kings transliteration). Reviewer view: accept English forms for the Writings. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, which are not retro-edited, and the four books must agree with each other. Record the genre split (narrative transliterated, poetry English) as deliberate, or settle it corpus-wide in one later decision.

'earth' at universal and cosmic sites (kol-hāʾāreṣ; ʾereṣ || tēbēl) is the reading of ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and the isaiah-woh precedent. 'land' is kept for territory (Prov 10:30; Job 37:13) and the stable 'wings of the land' (Job 37:3 = 38:13). Every site was checked. Agree with founder point C: promote the clause to central eretz in a later diff.

citations: Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament (1974), ch. 2
glossaryReview.reasoning: The 'life' / 'soul' split was checked at all six sites. 'life' where a life is delivered from death or forfeited (Ps 33:19 || 'keep them alive'; Prov 8:36 in the life/death antithesis), as in the Kings and Ezekiel overlays. ASV 'soul' is kept for the self (Ps 19:8; 33:20; 139:14; Prov 10:3), with the appetite sense in commentary. Direct is defensible: BDB lists both senses.

Applied correctly at every listed site. MT Psalm numbering was verified (superscription = v 1 in Pss 8, 19; run into v 1 in Ps 139). The one vowel-only exception at Ps 8:2 is declared and justified: the MT impv. tĕnâ has no syntax after ʾăšer. Eccl 3:21 keeps the Masoretic articular participles and fully records the interrogative reading of LXX, Vulgate, ASV, NRSV and NJPS. Non-blocking: add 'KJV' to the Eccl 3:21 clause as the English witness to the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so that the entry does not suggest that every English version departs from the MT.
appliesTo +3 ('land' sites only: Job 37:3, 13; Prov 10:30), verified; the 'earth' sites are correctly left to the overlay.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: All 32 lines checked. 10:13 keeps the ASV idiom 'void of understanding'; the canon's literal French is in a labelled note. No flags.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 205 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 16 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, the Leningrad source files, the overlays, the diff, the 2.83.0 base and the canon-quotation file before wave-w1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's list of the three canon-coincident lines (section 1) confirmed the two commentary revisions: at Job 37:18 and Prov 8:30 the notes cite only the canon's French, whose wording matches the line, and omit the canon's English ('the sky'; 'as one brought up with him'), which does not. Prov 8:22 already shows the correct treatment. The report's six-pair Ketiv/Qere count was independently confirmed.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-Ps-8:6-article-on-Elohim: Keep 'a little less than Elohim' without the article. The Hebrew mēʾĕlōhîm is anarthrous, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and Kings clause 2, and the reception note already gives the canon's 'the Elohim'. Differing from the canon here is useful evidence that the line follows the Hebrew.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-bene-(ha)adam: Accept 'the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human' for coherence with central ha-adam / ben-adam and GEN-WOH-11:5, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 ('the children of men') to it. The cost is stiff English at Prov 8:4, 31, and the Hebrew article on bĕnê (hā)ʾādām carries no difference in sense. If the founder prefers idiom, revert every plural site together to 'the sons of men' (string swap; drop the plural refIds from the ha-adam and ben-adam ops). Do not mix the two.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-eretz-cosmic-earth: Agree. Promote the 'earth' scope clause (isaiah-woh + Writings) to central eretz in a dedicated later diff, after the parallel appliesTo merges have landed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-proper-names: Accept English forms in the four Writings books. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, and the four books must agree. Record the corpus practice as genre-split (narrative transliterated, poetry and prophets English) or settle it in one corpus-wide decision. Do not leave it implicit.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-chesed-kindness: Confirm 'kindness' for solitary ḥesed now, before the Psalter grows (about 120 occurrences). It is the central wohChoice, consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and lexically sound (Glueck; Sakenfeld). The loyalty sense stays in commentary, and the fixed pair ḥesed wĕʾĕmet stays under chesed-v-emet.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-Job-37:18-clouds: No decision needed: 'clouds' rests on BDB/HALOT, KJV and stable job-woh 38:37, and 'strong' (not 'solid') keeps the line neutral. The reviewer asks for one transparency sentence (JOB-WOH-37:18 revise; shechaqim op revise): the canon's English edition reads 'the sky', so the canon is itself divided.

paragraphs.text: מִשְׁלֵ֗י שְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה (פ) בֵּ֣ן חָ֭כָם יְשַׂמַּח־אָ֑ב וּבֵ֥ן כְּ֝סִ֗יל תּוּגַ֥ת אִמּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father, but a foolish son is the grief of his mother.

notes.official: *mišlê šĕlōmōh* 'The proverbs of Solomon' heads the first Solomonic collection (10:1-22:16). The MT has a petucha (פ) inside the verse after the heading; it is kept in the Hebrew text, with no English marker. 'Solomon' is the English form, as in job-woh; 1 Kings woh has 'Shelomoh' (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-writings`).

paragraphs.text: לֹא־י֭וֹעִילוּ אוֹצְר֣וֹת רֶ֑שַׁע וּ֝צְדָקָ֗ה תַּצִּ֥יל מִמָּֽוֶת׃

i18n.en: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing, but righteousness delivers from death.

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־יַרְעִ֣יב יְ֭הוָה נֶ֣פֶשׁ צַדִּ֑יק וְהַוַּ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים יֶהְדֹּֽף׃

i18n.en: YHWH will not let the soul of the righteous go hungry, but he thrusts away the craving of the wicked.

notes.official: *lōʾ-yarʿîb YHWH nepeš ṣaddîq* 'YHWH will not let the soul of the righteous go hungry' (ASV). In the hunger image *nepeš* is the appetite (BDB *nepeš* 5); NRSV drops the noun ('the righteous'). The ASV 'soul' is kept for the self who hungers (`nefesh-scope-writings`). *hawwat rĕšāʿîm* 'the craving of the wicked' (ASV 'desire').

paragraphs.text: רָ֗אשׁ עֹשֶׂ֥ה כַף־רְמִיָּ֑ה וְיַ֖ד חָרוּצִ֣ים תַּעֲשִֽׁיר׃

i18n.en: Poor is the one who works with a slack hand, but the hand of the diligent makes rich.

notes.official: *rāʾš* 'Poor' (participle of *ryš*); *kap-rĕmiyyâ* 'a slack hand' (lit. 'a hand of deceit'); *ḥārûṣîm* 'the diligent'.

paragraphs.text: אֹגֵ֣ר בַּ֭קַּיִץ בֵּ֣ן מַשְׂכִּ֑יל נִרְדָּ֥ם בַּ֝קָּצִ֗יר בֵּ֣ן מֵבִֽישׁ׃

i18n.en: He who gathers in summer is a prudent son; he who sleeps in harvest is a son who causes shame.

paragraphs.text: בְּ֭רָכוֹת לְרֹ֣אשׁ צַדִּ֑יק וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְכַסֶּ֥ה חָמָֽס׃

i18n.en: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.

notes.official: *ûpî rĕšāʿîm yĕkasseh ḥāmās* 'but violence covers the mouth of the wicked' (ASV). Either noun can be the subject, and NRSV reads 'the mouth of the wicked conceals violence'. The ASV construal is kept here and in the identical v 11b.

paragraphs.text: זֵ֣כֶר צַ֭דִּיק לִבְרָכָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֖ם רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִרְקָֽב׃

i18n.en: The memory of the righteous is for a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.

notes.official: *zēker ṣaddîq librākâ* 'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing'; *yirqāb* 'will rot'.

paragraphs.text: חֲכַם־לֵ֭ב יִקַּ֣ח מִצְוֺ֑ת וֶאֱוִ֥יל שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט׃

i18n.en: The wise in heart will receive commandments, but a babbling fool will fall.

notes.official: *ʾĕwîl śĕpātayim yillābēṭ* 'a babbling fool will fall' (lit. 'a fool of lips'; ASV 'a prating fool shall fall'); *lbṭ* Niphal 'be thrown down' (Hos 4:14).

paragraphs.text: הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בַּ֭תֹּם יֵ֣לֶךְ בֶּ֑טַח וּמְעַקֵּ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכָ֗יו יִוָּדֵֽעַ׃

i18n.en: He who walks in integrity walks securely, but he who makes his ways crooked will be found out.

paragraphs.text: קֹ֣רֵֽץ עַ֭יִן יִתֵּ֣ן עַצָּ֑בֶת וֶאֱוִ֥יל שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט׃

i18n.en: He who winks the eye causes sorrow, and a babbling fool will fall.

notes.official: *qōrēṣ ʿayin* 'He who winks the eye', a gesture of malice (6:13). The second half repeats v 8b verbatim in the MT. The LXX has a different line ('but he who reproves boldly makes peace'), which NRSV adopts. The MT repeat is translated as in v 8 (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`).

paragraphs.text: מְק֣וֹר חַ֭יִּים פִּ֣י צַדִּ֑יק וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְכַסֶּ֥ה חָמָֽס׃

i18n.en: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.

notes.official: *mĕqôr ḥayyîm* 'a fountain of life'. The second half repeats v 6b; see there.

paragraphs.text: שִׂ֭נְאָה תְּעוֹרֵ֣ר מְדָנִ֑ים וְעַ֥ל כָּל־פְּ֝שָׁעִ֗ים תְּכַסֶּ֥ה אַהֲבָֽה׃

i18n.en: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all transgressions.

notes.official: *wĕʿal kol-pĕšāʿîm tĕkasseh ʾahăbâ* 'but love covers all transgressions' (quoted in 1 Pet 4:8; cf. Jas 5:20).

paragraphs.text: בְּשִׂפְתֵ֣י נָ֭בוֹן תִּמָּצֵ֣א חָכְמָ֑ה וְ֝שֵׁ֗בֶט לְגֵ֣ו חֲסַר־לֵֽב׃

i18n.en: On the lips of the one who has discernment wisdom is found, but a rod is for the back of the one who is void of understanding.

notes.official:
*bĕśiptê nābôn timmāṣēʾ ḥokmâ* 'On the lips of the one who has discernment wisdom is found'. *ḥăsar-lēb* (also v 21) is literally 'lacking heart', with *lēb* the seat of understanding; the line keeps the ASV sense, 'void of understanding'. *wĕšēbeṭ lĕgēw* 'but a rod is for the back'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 5) quotes the verse in a French wording that renders *ḥăsar-lēb* literally ('celui qui est privé de cœur', 'him who is deprived of heart'). The line gives the sense of the idiom; the literal form is recorded here.

paragraphs.text: חֲכָמִ֥ים יִצְפְּנוּ־דָ֑עַת וּפִֽי־אֱ֝וִיל מְחִתָּ֥ה קְרֹבָֽה׃

i18n.en: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool is a ruin close at hand.

notes.official: *yiṣpĕnû-dāʿat* 'store up knowledge'; *mĕḥittâ qĕrōbâ* 'a ruin close at hand'.

paragraphs.text: ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ מְחִתַּ֖ת דַּלִּ֣ים רֵישָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: The wealth of the rich is his strong city; the ruin of the poor is their poverty.

notes.official: *qiryat ʿuzzô* 'his strong city'; *mĕḥittat dallîm rêšām* 'the ruin of the poor is their poverty'.

paragraphs.text: פְּעֻלַּ֣ת צַדִּ֣יק לְחַיִּ֑ים תְּבוּאַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע לְחַטָּֽאת׃

i18n.en: The wage of the righteous is for life; the income of the wicked is for sin.

paragraphs.text: אֹ֣רַח לְ֭חַיִּים שׁוֹמֵ֣ר מוּסָ֑ר וְעוֹזֵ֖ב תּוֹכַ֣חַת מַתְעֶֽה׃

i18n.en: He who heeds instruction is on the way to life, but he who forsakes reproof goes astray.

paragraphs.text: מְכַסֶּ֣ה שִׂ֭נְאָה שִׂפְתֵי־שָׁ֑קֶר וּמוֹצִ֥א דִ֝בָּ֗ה ה֣וּא כְסִֽיל׃

i18n.en: He who hides hatred has lying lips, and he who utters slander is a fool.

paragraphs.text: בְּרֹ֣ב דְּ֭בָרִים לֹ֣א יֶחְדַּל־פָּ֑שַׁע וְחֹשֵׂ֖ךְ שְׂפָתָ֣יו מַשְׂכִּֽיל׃

i18n.en: In the multitude of words transgression is not lacking, but he who restrains his lips is prudent.

paragraphs.text: כֶּ֣סֶף נִ֭בְחָר לְשׁ֣וֹן צַדִּ֑יק לֵ֖ב רְשָׁעִ֣ים כִּמְעָֽט׃

i18n.en: The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; the heart of the wicked is worth little.

notes.official: *lēb rĕšāʿîm kimʿāṭ* 'the heart of the wicked is worth little' (lit. 'is as a little').

paragraphs.text: שִׂפְתֵ֣י צַ֭דִּיק יִרְע֣וּ רַבִּ֑ים וֶֽ֝אֱוִילִ֗ים בַּחֲסַר־לֵ֥ב יָמֽוּתוּ׃

i18n.en: The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of understanding.

notes.official: *yirʿû rabbîm* 'feed many' (*rʿh* 'shepherd'); *baḥăsar-lēb* 'for lack of understanding' (see v 13).

paragraphs.text: בִּרְכַּ֣ת יְ֭הוָה הִ֣יא תַעֲשִׁ֑יר וְלֹֽא־יוֹסִ֖ף עֶ֣צֶב עִמָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: The blessing of YHWH — it makes rich, and he adds no sorrow with it.

notes.official: *wĕlōʾ-yôsip ʿeṣeb ʿimmāh* 'and he adds no sorrow with it' (ASV, KJV, NRSV), with *ʿeṣeb* 'pain, sorrow' as in Gen 3:16-17. NJPS makes *ʿeṣeb* 'toil' the subject ('and no toil can increase it'). The ASV construal is kept.

paragraphs.text: כִּשְׂח֣וֹק לִ֭כְסִיל עֲשׂ֣וֹת זִמָּ֑ה וְ֝חָכְמָ֗ה לְאִ֣ישׁ תְּבוּנָֽה׃

i18n.en: Doing wickedness is like sport to a fool, and wisdom is so to a man of understanding.

notes.official: *kiśḥôq likĕsîl ʿăśôt zimmâ* 'Doing wickedness is like sport to a fool' (*zimmâ* 'wicked scheme'); 'and wisdom is so to a man of understanding' (the comparison is carried over from the first half, as in the ASV).

paragraphs.text: מְגוֹרַ֣ת רָ֭שָׁע הִ֣יא תְבוֹאֶ֑נּוּ וְתַאֲוַ֖ת צַדִּיקִ֣ים יִתֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: What the wicked dreads, that will come upon him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.

paragraphs.text: כַּעֲב֣וֹר ס֭וּפָה וְאֵ֣ין רָשָׁ֑ע וְ֝צַדִּ֗יק יְס֣וֹד עוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: When the storm passes, the wicked is no more, but the righteous is an everlasting foundation.

notes.official: *kaʿăbôr sûpâ* 'When the storm passes': *sûpâ* 'storm', as at Job 37:9 (ASV here 'whirlwind'). *yĕsôd ʿôlām* 'an everlasting foundation' (ASV).

paragraphs.text: כַּחֹ֤מֶץ ׀ לַשִּׁנַּ֗יִם וְכֶעָשָׁ֥ן לָעֵינָ֑יִם כֵּ֥ן הֶ֝עָצֵ֗ל לְשֹׁלְחָֽיו׃

i18n.en: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.

paragraphs.text: יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה תּוֹסִ֣יף יָמִ֑ים וּשְׁנ֖וֹת רְשָׁעִ֣ים תִּקְצֹֽרְנָה׃

i18n.en: The fear of YHWH adds days, but the years of the wicked will be shortened.

paragraphs.text: תּוֹחֶ֣לֶת צַדִּיקִ֣ים שִׂמְחָ֑ה וְתִקְוַ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים תֹּאבֵֽד׃

i18n.en: The hope of the righteous is gladness, but the expectation of the wicked will perish.

paragraphs.text: מָע֣וֹז לַ֭תֹּם דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֑ה וּ֝מְחִתָּ֗ה לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

i18n.en: The way of YHWH is a stronghold to the blameless, but ruin to the workers of iniquity.

paragraphs.text: צַדִּ֣יק לְעוֹלָ֣ם בַּל־יִמּ֑וֹט וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִשְׁכְּנוּ־אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: The righteous will never be moved, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.

notes.official: *ûrĕšāʿîm lōʾ yiškĕnû-ʾāreṣ* 'but the wicked will not dwell in the land': the settled land of 2:21-22, so the central `eretz` default 'land' (ASV 'the land'; `eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: פִּֽי־צַ֭דִּיק יָנ֣וּב חָכְמָ֑ה וּלְשׁ֥וֹן תַּ֝הְפֻּכ֗וֹת תִּכָּרֵֽת׃

i18n.en: The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but the perverse tongue will be cut off.

notes.official: *yānûb ḥokmâ* 'brings forth wisdom' (*nwb* 'bear fruit'); *lĕšôn tahpukôt tikkārēt* 'the perverse tongue will be cut off'.

paragraphs.text: שִׂפְתֵ֣י צַ֭דִּיק יֵדְע֣וּן רָצ֑וֹן וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable, but the mouth of the wicked, perverseness.

notes.official: *yēdĕʿûn rāṣôn* 'know what is acceptable'. The second half is verbless: 'but the mouth of the wicked, perverseness' (the ASV supplies '[speaketh]').
